note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are copied into the stack-allocated VLA Buffer; the trailing byte Buffer[Size] is NUL-terminated.
The stack input buffer is passed to the demangler; the output size argument is the input Size, while demangled is a fixed 4096-byte stack buffer.
mangled_cur is initialized to the start of the stack-allocated input buffer; out_end bounds all output writes.
A <source-name> length is parsed from attacker-controlled digits; an 'n' prefix makes the parsed number negative.
With the 'n' prefix sign == -1, so the returned length is negative (e.g. -20 for '_Zn20...'), which is not a valid <positive length number> but is accepted.
The parse cursor is advanced by the unchecked negative length, moving it before the start of the stack buffer; no check that length is positive or within the remaining input.
The bogus source name is accepted, so parsing continues into the optional <abi-tags> production with the out-of-bounds cursor.
First dereference of the out-of-bounds cursor (via ParseAbiTag), reading one byte before the stack-allocated input buffer and triggering an ASAN stack-buffer-overflow.
